# `Q-18-3` — Plot Rendered With Warnings

> A hephaestus plot document was rendered to SVG, but some of its features could not be expressed exactly.

## What this means

Quarto rendered the plot document to SVG and the page shows it, but
hephaestus's SVG backend reported that some part of the scene has no
exact SVG equivalent and was approximated or skipped. The message
lists each warning the backend raised.

## Why this happens

The SVG backend aims at editable output — text stays text, links stay
links — and a few things a rasterizer can draw have no faithful
vector form: certain blend modes and compositing operations, some
image sampling modes, and raster images when the build cannot decode
their format.

## How to fix

Usually nothing: the rendered plot is still correct in every respect
the warning does not name. If the degraded feature matters, change
the plot to avoid it, or export a raster image from the program that
produced the document and reference that instead.
